ideas_today.title: Self-Correcting SQL Agent with Guardrails
ideas_today.why: Demonstrates the ability to build reliable AI systems that interact with structured data while handling errors and security constraints, a critical requirement for enterprise LLM applications. Measured demand - LLMs: in 20% of 65 postings over 30 days (-14.5 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.65. AI Agents: in 23% of 65 postings over 30 days (-3.0 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.34. Data Analysis: in 15% of 65 postings over 30 days (-8.6 pp vs previous 7 days); trend score 0.00.
ideas_today.scope: Build a Python agent using LangChain or LlamaIndex that translates natural language queries into SQL. Implement a self-correction loop where the agent executes the query, catches syntax or runtime errors, and rewrites the SQL based on the error message. Add a validation layer to prevent destructive commands (DROP/DELETE) and log all interactions to a SQLite database for analysis.
success_metrics: Agent successfully corrects injected syntax errors in 90% of test cases without human intervention.
Zero execution of prohibited SQL commands during adversarial testing.
End-to-end latency for query generation and correction remains under 5 seconds.
